observation.visible_scene: A small green teardrop/pear-shaped object with a green calyx on its right side rests on a pale granular surface against a blurred gray wall; a tiny red-and-green tag hangs in the upper-right corner throughout. A dark, blurred hammer head enters from the top of the frame and descends onto the object. The watermark 'PK Slow Motion' is fixed at bottom-left.
visible_changes: Frames 1-5: the green object is stationary on the surface; only the hanging tag and background are visible.
Frames 6-8: a dark hammer head appears at top-center and moves downward toward the object (object still intact).
Frame 9: the hammer face contacts the top of the green object, which begins to compress/deform.
Frame 10: the object is flattened and spreads outward under the hammer face.
Frames 11-21: a cloud of white granular powder erupts and sprays outward/upward from the impact zone, carrying green fragments; the green body breaks into scattered pieces mixed with the powder.

Frames 22-41: the white powder cloud disperses and settles, green fragments remain scattered on the surface, and the hammer head gradually lifts/rebounds upward (its bottom edge rises from near the surface to a higher position by the last frame).

The green object undergoes deformation (squashing) then fragmentation (translation of pieces), while the hammer undergoes vertical translation (down then up). The background wall, surface horizon, and hanging tag stay in fixed positions, indicating a largely static camera.
outside_clip_unknowns: The exact identity of the green object and the white powder (surface granules vs. coating) is not determined.
The source, mass, or operator of the hammer, and the state of the scene before the clip begins or after it ends, are unseen.
Whether the powder cloud fully settles or the hammer continues rising beyond the last frame is not shown.
uncertain_details: Minor camera shake or zoom cannot be ruled out, but background evidence suggests the camera is essentially fixed.
The white spray is most consistent with surface granules kicked up by the impact, but its exact material is not verifiable.
The precise moment of first contact (between frames 8 and 9) and the start of the rebound (around frames 27-30) are approximate given the 0.08 s sampling.
